findings.failure_mechanism: authoritative contract identity was silently rewritten
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Collection tested a replacement name rather than the exact Markdown contract.
findings.repair_performed: Restored the exact name, regenerated modules, retained the architecture contradiction as explicit NON_APPLICABLE, and added equality meta-tests.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The Markdown/catalog set difference exposed one missing authoritative name and one invented name.

findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Leaked sockets/database state could be reported as a green example.
findings.repair_performed: Cleanup now attempts all resources and raises an ExceptionGroup containing every failure.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: LiveAdapter.close wrapped every close call in contextlib.suppress(Exception).
verification: source inspection and cleanup audit meta-record

findings.failure_mechanism: thread barrier synchronized call start but did not prove the target database/race boundary
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Scheduled contenders could execute sequentially while the test claimed a race invariant.
findings.repair_performed: Affected generated contracts are fail-closed until narrow production-disabled failpoints or authoritative database barrier observations are added.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: LiveAdapter.concurrent only places a barrier immediately before invoking each function.
verification: affected names are exhaustive in this audit and test-requirements.json

findings.failure_mechanism: tests and documentation trusted hard-coded catalog counts
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Catalog changes could make green completeness claims stale.
findings.repair_performed: All counts are recomputed from current Markdown, manifests, and collected node IDs.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The registry test embedded fixed existing/proposed/total literals.

findings.failure_mechanism: there was no exhaustive per-name audit/requirement join
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Systemic defects could be documented only with representative examples.
findings.repair_performed: Generated an exact route/status record for every name and full affected-name arrays for every systemic finding.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The authoritative catalog, generated collection, requirements, and audit affected-name sets are programmatically joined.

findings.failure_mechanism: protocol-v2 evidence was replayable and only case-hash bound
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Stale evidence from another physical execution could be relabelled with the same generated case.
findings.repair_performed: Protocol v3 requires an exact challenge envelope, current timestamps, unique evidence IDs, raw observation provenance, and rejects replays.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old protocol had no run ID, invocation ID, nonce, bounded collection time, or unique evidence ID.

findings.failure_mechanism: fault booleans and ChaosResult verdict were trusted as physical proof
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A no-op driver could claim injected=true/Passed while the target remained unaffected.
findings.repair_performed: Require two evidence sources, a fault-family-specific raw physical transition, raw ChaosEngine/ChaosResult UIDs, and independently recomputed request overlap.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The previous validator accepted driver-authored injection/window booleans without raw target transitions.

findings.failure_mechanism: name-derived generic predicates substituted for contract-specific business oracles
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A scenario-shaped response could satisfy parsed words without independently proving persisted business state.
findings.repair_performed: Removed false claims of implementation and fail-closed every unresolved contract; exact blockers remain in test-requirements.json.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The exhaustive legacy and semantic-override manifests identify every affected exact name.

findings.failure_mechanism: ChaosResult lookup and validation allowed a name-prefix fallback without exact ChaosEngine UID binding
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A stale or unrelated result with a colliding prefix could be accepted as the current invocation's Litmus state.
findings.repair_performed: Require exact chaosUID selection and independently bind the raw ChaosResult label to the raw ChaosEngine UID; add a hostile wrong-UID mutation.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The driver accepted name.startswith(engine_name) and the validator compared resource UIDs without checking the ChaosResult chaosUID label.

findings.failure_mechanism: an arbitrary configured command could bypass EXTERNAL_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED and reach name-derived predicates
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Unimplemented managed-cloud/control-plane contracts could green when a driver returned scenario-shaped protocol-v3 evidence without an exact independent oracle.
findings.repair_performed: Fail closed every unresolved implementation status regardless of command presence; only an IMPLEMENTED canonical requirement can invoke a driver.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Engine gated only SEMANTIC_ORACLE_REQUIRED, while ExternalContractDriver gated EXTERNAL_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED only when no command was configured.

findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Repeated examples did not vary a business dimension and inflated property counts.
findings.repair_performed: Converted native wrappers to one ordinary pytest invocation preserving the original oracle.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Every native wrapper executed the identical pytest node with only a hash-seed integer.
verification: pytest collection and registry source meta-tests

findings.failure_mechanism: blanket deadline=None and health-check suppression hid route-specific problems
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Hung live/external examples and fixture misuse could avoid Hypothesis feedback.
findings.repair_performed: Static/native tests are deterministic pytest; generated live/chaos/platform properties have bounded route-specific deadlines and one justified health suppression.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The same settings object was applied to static, native, live, and external routes.

findings.failure_mechanism: valid-sequence conservation strategies could shrink to retry/invalid-only no-op examples
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A green minimal example proved only that an untouched fixture conserved state; it did not cross an issue/accept/cancel transition.
findings.repair_performed: Require every generated example to begin with a real issue and then a valid accept or cancel before any generated continuation.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Strategy inspection showed an unconstrained operation list while the runner ignores symbols whose state preconditions are absent.
verification: compile verification; live execution requires the E2E deployment

findings.failure_mechanism: full-schema TRUNCATE had no cross-process exclusion
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Parallel workers or runs could erase one another's examples and contaminate shrinking.
findings.repair_performed: A session advisory lock is acquired before any reset and held for the runtime lifetime; unavailable lock fails/skips before mutation.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Database.reset truncates correctness-critical tables on a shared database.
verification: source inspection; live execution requires a provisioned PostgreSQL environment

findings.failure_mechanism: repository contained stopped pod-delete examples but no case-bound execution pipeline
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Chaos-named tests could not create or prove their prerequisites.
findings.repair_performed: Added pinned Dagger/Kind/supplied-cluster orchestration, pinned Litmus installation, 74 exact fault specifications, and executable independent oracles for pod-delete/loss/latency infrastructure contracts. Remaining named business oracles are fail-closed.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old manifests had engineState=stop and no Hypothesis/Dagger execution path.
verification: implemented Litmus family stages when a Docker/Kind runtime is available

findings.failure_mechanism: operator readiness assumed one Helm label dialect
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A healthy pinned Litmus installation using the legacy app=chaos-operator label could false-red before experiments began.
findings.repair_performed: Discover the actual deployment under either exact operator label and wait on each concrete deployment name with a bounded rollout deadline.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The pinned chart lineage has used both app and app.kubernetes.io/name conventions.
verification: compile/source verification; cluster execution requires a disposable Kubernetes runtime

findings.failure_mechanism: network effect probes used a host kubectl port-forward that could bypass the target pod interface
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Litmus could mutate pod eth0 while API-server port-forward traffic remained healthy, yielding false no-injection failures or measuring the wrong path.
findings.repair_performed: Execute every baseline, active, workload, and recovery HTTP probe inside the simulator pod against the encore-backend Service DNS, forcing traffic across the affected network path.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Topology tracing showed the runner's default probe was 127.0.0.1:14000 while network chaos targets the encore-backend pod.
verification: compile/source verification; physical execution requires disposable Kind/Litmus

findings.failure_mechanism: twenty random probes had to measure at least the exact configured packet-loss percentage
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A correctly injected 10% probabilistic loss false-reds frequently when fewer than two of twenty samples are lost.
findings.repair_performed: Use at least sixty-four bounded concurrent probes, require a clean baseline, independently verify exact parameter application, and require a conservative nonzero physical-effect threshold rather than equality to a probabilistic setting.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The binomial probability of observing below the exact 10% threshold with twenty samples is operationally large.

findings.failure_mechanism: workload overlap used a broad activation-to-cleanup timestamp without binding requests to physical-effect observations
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A request sent after the fault had already reverted could still fall before cleanup and be counted as crossing the failure window.
findings.repair_performed: For network faults, execute the exact generated workload as a subset of the raw effect-bearing probe batch; for pod deletion, require a clean baseline and at least one generated request that independently observed unavailability. Recompute exact request count and overlap in Python.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old crossing calculation compared only request timestamps to active_at and the later cleanup timestamp.

findings.failure_mechanism: implemented infrastructure contracts were described as business/database workloads and annotationCheck disagreed with the executable engine
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: The canonical mapping could not reconstruct the actual prerequisite or generated workload and falsely claimed database observations that the driver never collected.
findings.repair_performed: Emit exact infrastructure initial state, probes, effect-bound workload, raw observations, named oracle, and the executable annotation setting; retain business prerequisites only for unresolved business contracts.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Joining the four implemented records to litmus_driver.py exposed contract_specific_business_workload, seeded trade state, and annotation_check=true versus in-cluster probes and annotationCheck=false.

findings.failure_mechanism: route-integrity meta-test allowed the repository adapter only for categories 26 and 50
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Regenerating canonical routes correctly exposed every other live repository/database category as a false-red infrastructure failure.
findings.repair_performed: Validate every direct runner against its complete concrete adapter category set rather than a special-case category pair.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The regenerated meta suite failed first on category 80 even though both the mode registry and repository adapter support that category.

findings.failure_mechanism: standalone catalog verifier retained obsolete runner vocabulary and excluded direct repository/fault adapters
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: The canonical manifest could be internally consistent while the required zero-dependency verifier false-reded hundreds of valid routes.
findings.repair_performed: Use the canonical repo runner vocabulary, allow every direct adapter, and independently join each direct route to the category sets parsed from modes.py.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Strict verifier execution rejected repo for repository-static contracts, repo for live database contracts, and fault for live synchronized-fault contracts.

findings.failure_mechanism: native wrapper assigned the None return from require_repo as a path and passed unsupported context to assert_ok
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Every applicable native wrapper raised a harness TypeError before its original E2E oracle could execute.
findings.repair_performed: Use the validated RepoInspector.root path and support an optional failure context in CommandResult.assert_ok.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Source execution tracing showed require_repo returns None and CommandResult.assert_ok previously accepted no context argument.

findings.failure_mechanism: evidence protocol had no hostile testing
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Regression to a no-op, stale, mismatched, or non-overlapping driver could go unnoticed.
findings.repair_performed: Added no-op and every requested hostile mutation control.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: No prior test deliberately attempted the required adversarial evidence mutations.

findings.failure_mechanism: naming policy oracles included their own necessarily self-referential contract identities
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: The deterministic properties always false-red because their own names define the forbidden token patterns.
findings.repair_performed: Exclude only each policy contract's own identity while continuing to scan every other proposed name.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The implemented static subset failed twice with each policy contract itself as the sole offending name.

findings.failure_mechanism: test-reference oracle treated every test_* prose token as an executable pytest node selector
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Examples, historical reports, file stems, and reusable agent documentation produced false stale-reference failures.
findings.repair_performed: Scan executable workflow/action/script sources and extract only ::node and explicit pytest selector references; catalog equality remains independently verified.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Targeted execution reported unrelated prose from AGENTS.md, changes/, .o11y/, driver documentation, and Dagger fixtures.

findings.failure_mechanism: retry naming oracle used an incomplete token whitelist as a semantic business-effect classifier
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Valid names describing no resurrection, one durable result, bounded scheduling, or metric behavior false-red; the same heuristic could accept semantically vague names containing a magic token.
findings.repair_performed: Mark the contract SEMANTIC_ORACLE_REQUIRED until every retry-bearing name has a reviewed business-effect classification; strict mode now fails closed.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Targeted category-92 execution produced twenty immediate counterexamples to the token whitelist.

findings.failure_mechanism: crash naming oracle used a token whitelist as a semantic window/recovery classifier
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Valid fuzz-regression, no-crash pressure, and stale-lease transfer names false-red; magic window tokens could also false-green vague contracts.
findings.repair_performed: Mark the contract SEMANTIC_ORACLE_REQUIRED until crash-bearing names have a reviewed window and post-restart invariant mapping.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Targeted category-92 execution produced three counterexamples to the token whitelist.

findings.failure_mechanism: enum traceability oracle treated one textual token occurrence as proof of both success and rejection coverage
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Even a green result could not establish the two required test references; the current checkout also lacks token references for fifteen enum values.
findings.repair_performed: Mark the contract SEMANTIC_ORACLE_REQUIRED until an independent enum-to-success-and-rejection-test matrix is implemented.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Targeted category-91 execution exposed the missing values and source inspection exposed the one-occurrence oracle.

findings.failure_mechanism: database rejection contracts delegated exact invalid-row construction to generic external evidence
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A migration token or scenario-shaped response could not prove PostgreSQL rejected the named direct write or foreign-key violation without side effects.
findings.repair_performed: Mark every affected contract SEMANTIC_ORACLE_REQUIRED until schema-specific transactional mutation probes and persisted-state oracles exist.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: _database_live_check sends every category-26/50 contract to runtime.evidence rather than constructing its promised row mutation.

findings.failure_mechanism: merge-safety properties greened on rejection of deliberately invalid explicit destination IDs
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Ownership/not-found rejection never exercised successful automatic destination selection or observed where accepted items were persisted.
findings.repair_performed: Execute a successful accept with automatic destination selection and independently compare seller stack, escrow, buyer aggregate, and escrow-ID nonappearance in item_stack.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Both old branches assigned a forbidden destination and shared the generic rejection oracle.
verification: source/compile verification; live execution requires the E2E deployment

findings.failure_mechanism: implemented plan oracles fell back to generic external evidence when the required database column was absent
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A schema regression could bypass the authoritative PostgreSQL assertion instead of failing the property.
findings.repair_performed: Make both columns mandatory inputs to the live oracle and fail immediately when either authoritative field is absent.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Control-flow inspection found runtime.evidence fallbacks on missing intent and caused_by_capsuleer_id fields.
verification: compile verification; live execution requires the E2E deployment

findings.failure_mechanism: public-response checks omitted nested/camelized primary keys and did not place an actual transport secret near the error path
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A response could leak settlementBatchId or a nested primary key, while the error check merely searched an unrelated direct gRPC message for the word secret.
findings.repair_performed: Walk every nested response key, compare snake_case and lowerCamel primary-key forms, and drive an authenticated invalid UDP request while asserting the real signing secret is absent.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old key comparison used only top-level snake_case keys; the validation branch never used edge credentials.
verification: source/compile verification; live execution requires the E2E deployment

findings.failure_mechanism: terminal-state properties checked zero quantities or failed-step count without asserting the named terminal state
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: An OPEN batch/trade with zero quantities could satisfy the weaker oracle.
findings.repair_performed: Require the exact terminal state and a nonempty settlement-step observation before evaluating the named zero-state invariant.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Each branch omitted its COMPLETED or CANCELLED state assertion; the batch branch also allowed an empty step set.
verification: source/compile verification; live execution requires the E2E deployment

findings.failure_mechanism: command-identity uniqueness scanned a flat list without proving every required verification job supplied one
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: One well-formed identity could green even if other evidence-producing verification jobs omitted their identity entirely.
findings.repair_performed: Enumerate each evidence-producing job, require exactly one finish step with a nondefault identity, then prove job-level uniqueness.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old oracle extracted only command-identity text and never joined it to workflow jobs or their start/run/finish evidence steps.

findings.failure_mechanism: durable-channel oracles searched one repository-wide blob for both channel names and the absence of #ephemeral
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Either named consumer could be disconnected from its durable channel while unrelated source/config text kept both properties green.
findings.repair_performed: For each consumer, prove its exact source binding, topic declaration, and unique matching subscription in every NSQ self-host configuration; reject ephemeral names at each binding.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old branch did not join the consumer's NewSubscription call to its topic symbol, physical topic name, or each self-host NSQ configuration.

findings.failure_mechanism: cleanup evidence asserted target_effect_active=false after deleting resources without independently probing that the physical effect was absent
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A stale qdisc or partially recovered replica set could satisfy resource-absence checks and make cleanup/recovery properties green while impairment remained.
findings.repair_performed: Require every recovery probe to succeed, then run bounded post-cleanup probes, compare latency with the clean baseline, require full workload readiness, and only then record effect absence.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old cleanup branch populated the false value directly; pre-cleanup recovery also accepted only one successful probe out of three.
verification: compile verification; live Litmus execution remains environment-blocked

findings.failure_mechanism: independent validation did not bind the raw ChaosEngine target or physical pod transition to the declared selected resources
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A collector could claim selected EVE Trade labels at the top level while its raw engine or UID transition targeted an unrelated workload.
findings.repair_performed: Validate execution labels, exact raw appinfo, service account, experiment identity, and require physical transition UIDs to equal the independently label-validated selected resource UIDs.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old validator checked only the top-level selector and labels on claimed resources; it never inspected ChaosEngine appinfo or joined transition before_uids to selected UIDs.

findings.failure_mechanism: final chaos evidence accepted a Litmus phase of Running
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: An unfinished experiment with a prematurely populated verdict could pass phase validation without proving completion/revert semantics.
findings.repair_performed: Require Completed in both the top-level binding and raw ChaosResult before evaluating recovery or business oracles.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The phase guard explicitly accepted both Running and Completed despite validation occurring only after the driver's bounded completion wait.

findings.failure_mechanism: generated Litmus parameters were compared only with collector-authored applied_parameters, not the raw ChaosEngine environment
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A driver could inject a different duration/loss/latency than Hypothesis generated and still pass whenever the different fault happened to satisfy a weaker physical threshold.
findings.repair_performed: Parse the raw ChaosEngine environment, reject duplicate variables, bind every static/generated Litmus variable to the exact case/namespace, and bind start_offset_ms to raw engine creation and activation timestamps.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The old raw-engine validation checked neither experiment components nor environment values.

findings.failure_mechanism: recovery deadline evidence was not derived from the generated recovery_deadline_seconds value
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A collector could report an arbitrarily distant deadline and make a slow recovery satisfy the bounded-recovery check.
findings.repair_performed: Record recovery.started_at and require deadline_at to equal that timestamp plus the exact generated deadline before checking completion.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Validation compared completed_at with collector-supplied deadline_at but had no recovery start timestamp or duration join.

findings.failure_mechanism: Litmus manifest recorded only the 3.31.0 release while the pinned checkout's installed litmus-agent chart and operator images are 3.30.0
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Evidence provenance could misleadingly identify the release tag without identifying the chart and images actually installed for every chaos contract.
findings.repair_performed: Record release tag, installed chart/version, operator tag, and runner tag separately; make the installer reject any manifest or checked-out Chart.yaml mismatch.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The exact litmus-core-3.31.0 checkout declares litmus-agent chart 3.30.0 and chaos-operator appVersion 3.30.0.

findings.failure_mechanism: failed stages raised before being recorded and Dagger aborted before exporting failure artifacts
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: A red run could leave summary.json without the failed stage or keep the only evidence inside an exited container.
findings.repair_performed: Append stage evidence before raising, use ReturnType.ANY, export/retain artifacts, then propagate the nonzero status; add a nested-pytest failure canary.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Control-flow inspection followed the nonzero subprocess path through pytest_stage and Dagger with_exec.

findings.failure_mechanism: integration credentials were forwarded as ordinary Dagger environment values
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Database URLs and edge signing secrets could appear in DAG metadata or diagnostic output.
findings.repair_performed: Forward every externally supplied integration setting through Dagger Secret objects consumed directly by the Dagger execution container.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Source inspection found all FORWARDED_ENV values passed through with_env_variable.

findings.failure_mechanism: supplied-cluster mode unnecessarily depended on a host Unix Docker socket and nested Docker
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: The advertised first-class fallback could not run on hosts where nested Docker/Unix-socket mounting is unavailable.
findings.repair_performed: Run supplied-cluster orchestration directly in a Dagger container with an isolated kubeconfig and exported artifact directory; scope the Docker socket requirement only to disposable Kind.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Both Kind and supplied branches passed through the same unconditional Docker socket check.
verification: compile/source verification; live supplied-cluster execution requires an external disposable cluster

findings.failure_mechanism: Dagger source root was derived from the caller's current working directory
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Invoking the documented script from its own directory or a CI wrapper directory could mount only that subtree and make every later build/test stage fail or inspect the wrong files.
findings.repair_performed: Resolve the checkout root from pipeline.py's stable repository location and add a meta-test independent of the test process working directory.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: A direct invocation from property-tests/infra resolved REPO_ROOT to that directory rather than the checkout root.

findings.failure_mechanism: Kind mode validated a Dagger source snapshot but executed tests from a second mutable host bind mount inside nested Docker
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Concurrent host edits or mount/path differences could make structural evidence and runtime evidence describe different source trees.
findings.repair_performed: Copy the validated Dagger Directory into the host-networked Kind runner through the Docker API instead of bind-mounting REPO_ROOT, then copy and export failure artifacts through Dagger.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Control-flow inspection found validate_source consuming the Dagger Directory while docker run mounted REPO_ROOT independently as /src.

findings.failure_mechanism: category-78 parser fuzz contracts were marked implemented without a parser fuzz runner
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: The repository dispatcher fell through to external evidence, so development mode could skip tests advertised as implemented.
findings.repair_performed: Classified the exact contracts as SEMANTIC_ORACLE_REQUIRED until a real parser fuzz harness and acceptance/crash oracle exist.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Executing the implemented static subset produced skips for all category-78 contracts; source inspection confirmed no category-78 branch.

findings.failure_mechanism: execution ignored the canonical per-contract runner and re-derived dispatch from category
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Contracts deliberately classified static inside historically fault/edge categories would enter the wrong adapter if their fail-closed gate were resolved.
findings.repair_performed: Dispatch from the canonical requirement runner and make repo the same executable route identifier in generation, registry validation, and engine execution.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Engine source called modes.runner_for(category) even though the exhaustive requirement record already carried the unique semantic runner.

findings.failure_mechanism: direct live database contracts were assigned the trade adapter, which has no category-26/50 handler
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: The wrapper would raise an unhandled trade category before reaching either a database probe or a fail-closed oracle.
findings.repair_performed: Route repository/database categories to the repo adapter even when their physical mechanism is DIRECT_LIVE; retain fail-closed status until the live probes exist.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Joining implemented DIRECT_LIVE requirements to trade_contracts.handlers exposed every affected route as impossible.

findings.failure_mechanism: direct-live fault categories were assigned the trade adapter instead of the fault adapter
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Resolving any affected fail-closed semantic blocker would make execution enter an unsupported trade category rather than its synchronized fault driver.
findings.repair_performed: Route direct-live categories 36 and 64 through the fault adapter and validate direct routes against the complete fault category set.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The strengthened route-integrity meta-test failed on category 64 and manifest inspection found the same defect in category 36.

findings.failure_mechanism: recursive repository scans traversed ignored generated dependency trees
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Static properties could false-red on vendored Terraform provider modules rather than EVE Trade source.
findings.repair_performed: Centralized repository traversal exclusions for .git, .agents, .codex, .o11y, .terraform, virtual environments, Dagger caches, node_modules, target, and Python caches.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The secret-variable contract failed on .terraform provider source; the same contract passed after excluding generated/cache roots.
verification: targeted secret-variable property passed after repair
targeted catalog-reference property no longer scans .agents

findings.failure_mechanism: Kubernetes properties omitted the production orchestration tree and allowed an empty workload set
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: CI YAML made the document list nonempty while pod_specs yielded nothing, so universal security assertions passed vacuously.
findings.repair_performed: Render every leaf Kustomize target from the real orchestration tree, reject empty workload/container sets, and evaluate effective pods rather than patch fragments.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: Path inspection showed kubernetes_documents lacked distributed-backend/orchestration/kubernetes; control-flow inspection showed no pod-count assertion.
verification: targeted Windows render attempted; kubectl child process was blocked by local filesystem policy

findings.failure_mechanism: generated fault values were serialized but not proven applied
findings.false_green_or_false_red_risk: Shrinking could change evidence labels without changing the physical experiment.
findings.repair_performed: Litmus strategies are generated from the canonical safe domain; the driver applies every value to Litmus/workload configuration and the validator checks exact applied parameters. Unsupported business contracts remain fail-closed.
findings.reproduction_or_proof: The previous driver only checked case_sha256 and driver booleans.
